text: player
A World With You
Since coming back from the beach, I've been feeling feverish and weak...
Home
I must have caught a cold... Guess I'll have to turn down the mahjong club's invitation.
My eyes feel so heavy... I need more sleep.
Huh? Was I expecting a delivery today?
When I open the door, I find a familiar face – Yui, carrying two enormous shopping bags, one in each hand.
Yui...? What brings you here?
Yui Yagi
I saw your message in the group chat.
How are you feeling now? Are you okay?
I'm alright, my fever's gone down. Thanks for coming to check on me.
Your face... still looks a bit pale.
Really? Well, I've only just recovered, so...
What's in all those bags anyway?
Ingredients.
Hmm?
I thought I'd cook some nourishing food for you.
That way, you'll get better soon.
Ah, that's... really kind of you...
I never imagined Yui would come to cook for me. This girl who rarely shows emotions actually has such a thoughtful, caring side...
I invite her in, take the shopping bags, and peek inside to see what she's brought.
Just one glance at these overstuffed shopping bags gives me a bad feeling...
One is packed with green onions, chives, and both white and red onions.
The other is filled with leeks, garlic, and...
Uh... what's this long, thin vegetable?
Victory onion.
That's an awful lot of onions...!
I read that they are good for a cold, so I bought a whole variety of them.
Eating all these should help cure your cold, right?
Ah, well... Technically... I guess.
Oh no, this is bad! I nearly forgot – I can't let her cook! The memory of what happened last time we went to the supermarket is still all too fresh in my mind.
But seriously, what kind of dish would use all these ingredients?
Actually, I just finished lunch, so I'm quite full at the moment.
But thanks for bringing all these ingredients. I'll keep them for later.
I'm sorry... I know you went out of your way for me, but I really can't eat anything more right now.
After putting all the ingredients in the refrigerator, I return to the front door.
Yui's face doesn't show much, but observing carefully, I can tell she's slightly disappointed.
Well... How about...
How about we go for a walk instead? I've been stuck in bed for days and my muscles are all stiff.
Okay.
It's subtle, but her eyes seem to light up a bit.
Where would you like to go?
Éternité.
They have excellent coffees. You've probably heard of it.
Oh, I know that place. I go there a lot.
At least they won't serve any bizarre culinary creations there...
Stepping into the familiar coffee shop, I casually greet the young manager, Reina Nanami.
Éternité
Unlike my usual order, today we both get regular iced coffee at Yui's insistence.
Do you visit here often?
Yes, every week.
You're definitely a regular then... are you a big coffee fan?
I believe that... coffee is a science.
Oh? A science?
For starters, just the measurement of coffee beans is critical.
The slightest difference can drastically alter the taste. That's why when making coffee, you need to measure the beans precisely to the gram.
And the grinding process demands even more care.
You can't grind coffee beans too fast or too slow. You need to maintain the perfect speed to prevent excess heat from affecting the beans' flavor profile.
Plus, depending on the grind size, you'll need to use different brewing methods.
Beyond that, water temperature and pouring technique also influence the final result.
It's exactly like a scientific experiment... where every reagent must be precisely measured.
Yes, but this shop does everything perfectly.
That's why their iced coffee is so good.
I see!
Although I still have my doubts about Yui's taste in food, after that detailed explanation, I'm actually eager to try the coffee she's recommended.
Reina Nanami
Your iced coffees, please enjoy.
I thank Reina and pick up the cup.
Just one sip and I immediately understand why Yui recommended it so highly.
It's really good.
A cool touch on the tongue, then a bloom of rich coffee aroma, leaving no sharp acidity or bitterness in its wake...
I never imagined it would be this good. Though I'm no coffee expert, I can tell it's exceptional from the very first taste.
Yes, it's excellent.
Senpai? Why are you looking like that?
Nothing, I'm just a bit emotional.
Yui has surprisingly good taste in coffee. Or more accurately, she's extremely knowledgeable about it.
And, her knowledge is extensive. Given the chance, she could probably talk about coffee until nightfall.
I thought Yui and I had become quite close, but I'm still discovering new aspects of her...
When did you start to love coffee?
Probably since I was young.
Before my parents passed away, they often taught me about coffee.
Everything from brewing methods to rare bean varieties and even cultivation techniques.
Did you know?
In some regions, people crack a whole raw egg – shell and all – into the ground coffee before brewing.
Those living near deserts make their coffee by brewing it on hot sand.
And in some other places, people drink a mix of coffee and black tea.
All of these... are things my parents taught me.
That's fascinating...
For someone usually so quiet, Yui is being remarkably talkative today.
While her face shows little emotion, her genuine enthusiasm for sharing is clear.
Have you ever thought about opening your own coffee shop?
You've learned so much from your parents.
For just a moment, a shadow seems to cross Yui's eyes.
It's so subtle that you would totally miss it if you weren't paying attention.
Yui?
Somehow, the coffee I make never tastes good.
That's surprising. I would've thought Yui had a great palate for coffee.
What's your usual coffee-making process? Maybe we can troubleshoot together?
Well... I start by carefully selecting the coffee beans.
Mm-hmm.
Then I weigh the beans down to the gram. When grinding, I maintain the perfect speed so no excess heat transfers to the beans...
So far, so good?
Lastly, to enhance the aroma, I add a bit of fish powder to the ground coffee.
Hm-hmm.
Hold on, WHAT?!
I normally use primarily bonito, but I find that mixing in some flying fish and sardine powder gives the coffee a richer flavor profile.
As the final touch, I add a bit of that new seasoning Mirai just developed. I don't know what's in it, but she said to use about two tablespoons...
S-stop right there!
Your process was flawless until the grinding! Where did all these weird ingredients come from?!
After grinding, you should just brew it! Don't add anything strange!
I see. Are you suggesting I need to learn about "minimalism"?
I never thought of it like that. Thank you.
Oh, uh... no problem... That's just what people would usually expect, I guess?
Yes, I miss them dearly.
I'm sorry... I shouldn't have brought this up.
No, it's okay. I've already accepted that they're gone.
I see. You're really strong, Yui.
What were your parents like?
Like I said before, they were both scientists. I think they met at the laboratory where they worked.
Dad was usually quiet and didn't smile much. But he was actually very gentle and sometimes said quirky things to make us all laugh.
(Yui's personality probably comes from her father.)
Mom was outgoing and had many friends. She was always smiling brightly, and whenever I helped with chores, she'd pat my head...
Sounds like they were complete opposites.
Perhaps that's exactly why they got along so well.
Yeah, perhaps.
Yui sits there with the straw in her mouth, gazing at me without a word.
Is there something on my face again? I check with my hand, but don't find anything.
Hmm... Is everything okay?
Yeah, it's nothing.
I still can't figure out what she's thinking. But somehow, she looks happier than usual.
After leaving Éternité, we keep walking and eventually come to a pathway along the river.
Riverside Walkway
The breeze is refreshing against my face. Though my cold just cleared up a bit, I feel like I could walk for miles.
Senpai, you're looking better.
Really? I do feel much more energetic now.
It's probably the coffee.
Yui appears to smile briefly, though the light reflecting off the water makes it difficult to tell for certain.
Sometimes, I wonder...
...what life would be like if my parents were still around.
Yui leans against the railing, her eyes narrowing slightly as she looks at the river.
I'm in college now, so I probably wouldn't be holding their hands walking home anymore. I might even be seeing them less and less frequently.
But no matter how old they got, we'd still be just as close to each other. We'd walk along rivers like this, having pleasant conversations.
Back home, my father would brew a pot of coffee, and we'd all share stories about our day.
I would just sit quietly, listening to their conversation.
Just listening would be enough to make me happy.
Senpai...
Yui turns to face me.
Have I really never moved on?
I thought I'd moved beyond the pain of losing them, but...
Every time I look back on the past, I just think... I can't keep being like this.
There's nothing wrong with that.
What?
This might not be my place, but there's no need to rush past your grief.
Sometimes it's okay not to be strong. There's nothing wrong with dwelling on memories of them.
Maybe. Thank you.
I join Yui at the railing, leaning against it as she does.
As the sun begins to set, its light dances across the water, making the gem-like sparkles even more radiant.
My parents were studying something about "parallel universes," I think.
Parallel universes? That sounds like science fiction.
I'm not entirely sure either. They didn't tell me much about it.
Are those like different universes from our own?
It sounds incredible... could something like that actually exist?
I don't know.
Senpai, if there were another world, would you want to visit it?
Probably not... I wouldn't know if I could ever return.
Hmm... it does sound interesting, I'd like to check it out.
That choice is so you.
And what about you? Would you want to visit another world?
I'd rather cherish the world I'm in.
Because right now...
...you're right here with me, aren't you?
In a quiet moment, Yui's eyes meet mine.
I look into her eyes that shimmer with the reflected sunset.
Why don't we start a coffee shop together?
I want to cherish this world that has you in it, too.
Haha, just kidding, we're not really... whoa?!
Before I can finish my sentence, Yui suddenly grips my hand tightly.
Her eyes are sparkling even more intensely now.
But somehow, I have a bad feeling about it!
Senpai!
Wh-what is it?!
With you by my side, I think I could become the ultimate coffee master...!
Holding my hand, Yui breaks into a run.
I don't know our destination, but her determined pace is almost intimidating.
Uh... what is this place?
My go-to apothecary shop.
Your go-to... apothecary shop?
The old shop is filled with an unusual herbal smell.
Are all these... medicinal materials?
Uh... why an apothecary shop? I thought we were talking about coffee?
Medicinal coffee.
Huh?
This is the perfect answer I've found after years of research.
Coffee tastes good, and herbal medicines are good for health. So by combining the two, we create the perfect drink... Q.E.D.
Q.E.D. what?! That's not how this works! And what about the taste? Won't these additions completely ruin the flavor?!
Shop Owner
*cough* Who's making all this noise? Can't even let an old woman get some peace and quiet...
An elderly woman in a black robe appears from behind the counter.
Though it's not so bad hearing someone else's voice in this shop for a change... *cough*
Anyway, what was the young lady talking about?
Medicinal coffee? Now that sounds intriguing.
Let me help you pick the herbs. I'll give you a discount. *cough*
And, hehe... I'd like to taste the final product too.
Of course!
Yui? That glint in your eyes is rather alarming...
There's no stopping her now. She's completely in her own world.
Lost in discussion, Yui and the shop owner fill a paper bag with all sorts of bizarre ingredients.
Not even the most experimental barista would consider these as coffee ingredients...
Sorry to keep you waiting.
Oh, are you done?
Yes. I'm really excited about today's experiment.
What? Today?
Yes, right now. I'll head straight to your place and make it for you.
Uhhh, m-maybe...?!
While Yui's face doesn't show much, it's clear she's truly looking forward to brewing this for me.
That look... is just impossible to turn down.
It'll be fine... right?
On the way home, I try so hard to convince myself, leaving everything to fate, and her hands.
The moment the words left my mouth, I realized how embarrassing they were. I can already feel my face starting to burn.
(Is Yui going to think I'm ridiculous?)
Looking at her, I see Yui is quietly staring at the ground.
(Is she... embarrassed? Or disappointed?)
Yui's face is as expressionless as usual, but it's making me anxious that I can't tell what she's feeling right now.
Senpai...
Hm?
Since we met, has your life changed at all?
Yui asks with her head still down.
I'd say my world has become much wider.
You're exaggerating.
Not at all. All the incredible things you've shared have changed how I see the world.
And life has become so much more fascinating since I met you.
Senpai...
Yui keeps her head lowered.
You're such an unusual person. Do you know that?
Huh? Where did that come from?
I wouldn't say I'm that unusual...
Yui finally lifts her head, with what seems to be a faint smile.
It's really just the faintest smile, so subtle that only someone who's spent time with her and truly cares would notice it.
Your words seem ordinary, but they feel completely different from anyone else's.
That's why I'm always drawn to you.
And yes, I've changed a lot too, since meeting you.
I've become curious about myself.
I want to learn more about myself.
The breeze ruffles Yui's long hair as she turns her face away.
...Did you know?
I recently found out I have a serious weakness.
There's often a gap between what I think tastes good and what others enjoy.
But that's never been the case with coffee.
I'm sorry I never mentioned it.
Don't worry, it was pretty obvious.
I fight back the urge to point that out, searching my mind for something more supportive to say.
Let me help you work on this weakness.
Really? But can I really overcome it?
Absolutely, I promise.
Hehe.
This time, I'm sure Yui is actually smiling.
I definitely didn't imagine it.
We'll start by cooking together.
You've already bought all those ingredients, right? Even if they're nothing but onions.
Just curious, what were you planning to cook?
Burger steak.
Wait, what?
What?
It seems our journey to overcome this weakness will be long and difficult...
But I'm confident we'll succeed someday.
Walking home with Yui by my side, I keep telling myself it'll be okay.
But really, what are we going to do with all those onions she bought?
Hearing this, Yui's eyes grow wide.
This is the first time I've seen such a dramatic change in her expression.
Ah.
A glimmer of light trails down her cheek.
It's only when I see Yui hurriedly wipe at the corner of her eye that I realize it was a tear.
I-I'm sorry...
Matter can't be created or destroyed, it only changes form.
Um?
Yui turns away and starts speaking, her voice slow but determined.
But there's a faint quiver in her voice.
This is a basic principle of physics. Did you know about this?
I think... I've heard something like that before.
Just as I say it, I suddenly remember Yui mentioning her parents were scientists and how much she misses them.
I might not know anything about physics research, but I can tell she's trying to get something very important across to me.
Even when matter burns to ash, it transforms back into the very particles that will go on to form new substances, forever drifting through our world. That's how physics works.
So in a way, my parents are still part of this world.
Maybe the particles that once made them have just changed into something else, still present in this world.
Maybe...
What brought us together... could actually be them, now transformed into particles, drifting around us.
That's a beautiful way to look at it...
Am I getting too philosophical all of a sudden?
No, not at all.
Another teardrop slides down Yui's face.
I stay quiet, remaining by her side.
At a moment like this... it would be insensitive to stare at her tearful face.
Instead, I stand beside her, quietly sharing this view with her.
This beautiful world, this special moment... it's all a gift from those who are now woven into the particles of everything around us.
Yes?
Nothing. The sunset... it's beautiful, isn't it?
Yes, it is.
Without realizing it, we've already started walking forward.
Our destination is clear. Yui's ingredients are still waiting in my fridge.
Looking forward to our journey together, senpai.
A smile blooms on Yui's face, and it feels like my whole world just comes to a sudden, silent halt.
For them... for the particles still watching over us, I will protect this smile.
(Knock, knock)
So, it seems like once you get into the details, there's always more to discover with coffee, huh?
Th-the ultimate...?
The shelves are lined with containers holding various dried plants and animal parts.
Well, it is medicine, after all. At the very least, it should help with my cold.
Well, how should I put it?
Let's see... what are you planning to cook?
I thought so too. Though I'm just taking it literally...
It's a bit embarrassing to be stared at so directly from this close, but I know I shouldn't look away.
